display.purpose: The name in the masthead, once. Print: 26pt.

headline.purpose: Station headings (one per section), each carrying a ring on the line. Print: 15pt.

title.purpose: Role and degree titles inside stops; project titles in timetable rows run at 1.2rem. Organisation names inside a title are weight 800.

lead.purpose: The one-line position under the name, capped at 34em. Narrow screens: 1.1rem.

body.purpose: All reading text, capped at the 68ch measure. Narrow screens: 16px. Print: 11pt at 1.4.

label.purpose: Buttons (uppercase, 0.1em). The sticky strip uses the same face at 0.08em, weight 400 for links and 600 for the current station name.

meta.purpose: Dates, definition terms, feed meta, stack lines and the colophon (12.5 to 13px). Never running prose.

shadows.name: portrait-lift
shadows.purpose: The masthead portrait only. Removed in print.

shadows.name: marker-lift
shadows.purpose: The 12px ink marker that rides the line. Hidden in print.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The long ease-out for the marker's travel and the station ring's scale.

motion.name: marker-travel
motion.purpose: The marker sliding along the line to the current station. The page's only motion event; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: ring-arrive
motion.purpose: The current station ring scaling to 1.12 when the marker arrives.

motion.name: button-fill
motion.value: background-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease

motion.name: scroll
motion.purpose: Anchor jumps from the strip; auto under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below it: rail 40px, line 5px, rings 18px, gutters 16px, body 16px, every two-column row collapses to one.

layout.lineTail: 96px below the last station, stopping 40px short of the bottom

components.css: .ds-track { position: relative; height: 120px; width: 40px; } .ds-track::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 17px; width: 6px; background: var(--line, #C8102E); border-radius: 0 0 3px 3px; } .ds-marker { position: absolute; z-index: 2; left: 14px; top: 0; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--ink, #15181B); transform: translateY(var(--marker-y, 0px)); transition: transform 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.19, 1, 0.22, 1); box-shadow: 0 2px 6px -1px rgba(21, 24, 27, 0.4); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-marker { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The site reads a career the way a Copenhagen S-tog or Metro diagram reads a route: one continuous red line down the left margin, a station ring at every section, branch-line stops for every role and degree, and a marker that shows the reader where they are. The CV is the document; the diagram is the frame that carries the eye down it. Everything else is paper: near-white cool ground, black-green ink, 1px hairlines, and a great deal of unprinted space between stations.

Density is editorial, not dashboard. One reading column of 68ch sits right of the rail; dates and codes are set in tabular mono in a narrow left-hand column so they line up like a timetable. The page uses one hue only. Red is the line and everything that belongs to it (station rings, stop dots, links, the primary button, focus and selection); state is carried by the form of a mark (filled, hollow, dashed, ink-filled) rather than by a second colour. The system refuses the centred hero portrait over a grid of same-size project cards and the LaTeX-paper CV look.

Motion is a single event: the marker travels the line to the current station on scroll (0.9s, a long ease-out), and the ring it reaches grows by 12%. Nothing else moves beyond a 150ms button fill. Light and dark schemes share every rule and swap only the seven surface and ink values; print strips the chrome and leaves the line, the rings and the ruled rows on white.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous 6px signal-red line in an 88px left rail, with 22px station rings at every section heading.
One hue: red for the line and its belongings, ink for everything else; state as a mark (filled / hollow / dashed / ink-filled), never a second colour.
Overpass for display and body at 400/600/800, Overpass Mono for dates, codes and labels; no italics anywhere.
Hairline rules (1px) and vast vertical space (72px between stations) instead of cards, boxes or shadows.
0-radius buttons and 50% rings: squares for actions, circles for places on the line.
One motion moment: the marker sliding down the line; reduced-motion disables it.
Three renderings from one stylesheet: light, dark, and print (the page is the CV).

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Signal red belongs to the line. It may appear on the line, on a ring or dot that sits on the line, on a link, on the primary button, and on focus and selection. It never fills a panel, tints a background, or colours a heading.

rules.name: The Mark, Not Hue Rule
rules.body: State is carried by the form of a mark, never by a second colour: a past stop is a filled red dot, a current stop is a hollow ring (surface fill, red border), a planned stop is a dashed outline, the terminus is ink-filled. Adding a green, amber or blue to say "current" or "planned" breaks the diagram.

rules.name: The No Italics Rule
rules.body: `em` renders as weight 600, never slanted. Book titles, foreign words and emphasis are all weight. This holds in print too.

rules.name: The Mono Is for Measures Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono carries dates, years, codes, tech stacks, labels, meta notes and the colophon. It never sets a sentence of running prose and never exceeds 13px.

rules.name: The Rail Rule
rules.body: The left rail belongs to the line. Nothing but the line, the station rings and the marker is drawn there; text, images and rules start at the content edge.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: Only the portrait and the marker cast shadows. Every other edge is a 1px hairline or nothing.

rules.name: The Square Actions, Round Stations Rule
rules.body: Buttons and containers are 0-radius; anything that marks a point on the line is a full circle. There is no 4px, 8px or pill radius anywhere in the system.

dos: Do keep signal red (`#C8102E` light, `#E8364F` dark) for the line, rings, dots, links, the primary button, focus and selection only (The One Red Rule).
Do draw state with the form of a mark: filled past, hollow current, dashed planned, ink-filled terminus (The Mark, Not Hue Rule).
Do set every date, year, code, stack line and label in Overpass Mono at 12 to 13px, and keep `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on.
Do separate content with 1px hairlines (`#C9CBC9`) and vertical space (72px between stations, 22/26px row padding, 12px grid rows), never with boxes.
Do keep all buttons at 0 radius with mono uppercase labels at 0.1em and 40px height, and all marks on the line at 50% radius.
Do keep the reading column at 68ch to the right of the 88px rail, with the line centred 40px into the rail.
Do ship every scheme from the same rules: dark swaps only the seven colour tokens; print hides the strip, feed, marker and colophon and prints the line on white.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: the marker jumps and nothing transitions.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, a tinted panel, a gradient, or a coloured heading; ink and one red are the whole palette.
Don't round a rectangle (no 4px, 8px or pill corners on buttons, rows, strips or inputs) and don't square a station ring.
Don't add cards, drop shadows or elevation to content; only the portrait and the marker may cast a shadow (The Two Shadows Rule).
Don't place anything but the line, its rings and the marker inside the left rail.
Don't add motion beyond the marker's travel, the ring's 1.12 scale and the 150ms button fill.
Don't set running prose in Overpass Mono or let mono exceed 13px.
Don't use icon fonts or glyph icons; the only icon is the inline 11px external-link SVG stroke in `currentColor`.
